arxiv-1808-06258.title: Universal Proof Theory: Semi-analytic Rules and Uniform Interpolation
arxiv-1808-06258.creator: Amirhossein Akbar Tabatabai, Raheleh Jalali
arxiv-1808-06258.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Amirhossein Akbar Tabatabai, Raheleh Jalali. In [ 7 ] and [ 8 ] , Iemhoff introduced a connection between the existence of a terminating sequent calculi of a certain kind and the uniform interpolation property of the super-intuitionistic logic that the calculus captures. In this paper, we will generalize this relationship to also cover the substructural setting on the one hand and a much more powerful class of rules on the other.

arxiv-2205-15779.title: Maximum likelihood kinetic Sunyaev Zel’dovich velocity reconstruction
arxiv-2205-15779.creator: Dagoberto Contreras 1, Fiona McCarthy 2,3,4, Matthew C. Johnson 1,3
arxiv-2205-15779.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dagoberto Contreras 1, Fiona McCarthy 2,3,4, Matthew C. Johnson 1,3. The kinetic Sunyaev Zel’dovich (kSZ) effect, cosmic microwave background (CMB) temperature anisotropies induced by the scattering of CMB photons from free electrons, will be measured by near-term CMB experiments at high significance. By combining CMB temperature anisotropies with a tracer of structure, such as a galaxy redshift survey, previous literature introduced a number of techniques to reconstruct the radial velocity field.

arxiv-2211-14159.title: Shape optimization of superconducting transmon qubit for low surface dielectric loss
arxiv-2211-14159.creator: Sungjun Eun, Seong Hyeon Park, Kyungsik Seo, Kibum Choi, Seungyong Hahn
arxiv-2211-14159.description: Abstract Surface dielectric loss of superconducting transmon qubit is believed as one of the dominant sources of decoherence. Reducing surface dielectric loss of superconducting qubit is known to be a great challenge for achieving high quality factor and a long relaxation time ( T 1 T_{1} ).

arxiv-2303-03326.title: Keep It Simple: CNN Model Complexity Studies for Interference Classification Tasks
arxiv-2303-03326.creator: Taiwo Oyedare ⋆ , Vijay K. Shah † , Daniel J. Jakubisin ⋆‡ , Jeffrey H. Reed ⋆
arxiv-2303-03326.description: Abstract The growing number of devices using the wireless spectrum makes it important to find ways to minimize interference and optimize the use of the spectrum. Deep learning models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have been widely utilized to identify, classify, or mitigate interference due to their ability to learn from the data directly.

arxiv-2402-17912.title: Magnetocaloric performance of RE 5 Pd 2 In 4 (RE = Tb-Tm) compounds
arxiv-2402-17912.creator: Altifani Rizky Hayyu, Stanisław Baran, Andrzej Szytuła
arxiv-2402-17912.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Altifani Rizky Hayyu, Stanisław Baran, Andrzej Szytuła. Magnetocaloric performance of the RE 5 Pd 2 In 4 (RE = Tb-Tm) rare earth compounds has been investigated using measurements of magnetization in the function of temperature and applied magnetic field.

arxiv-2403-19450.title: Observational Constraints on the Maximum Masses of White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, and Exotic Stars in Non-Minimal Derivative Coupling Gravity
arxiv-2403-19450.creator: M. D. Danarianto a,b, I. Prasetyo c,d, A. Suroso e, B. E. Gunara e, A. Sulaksono b
arxiv-2403-19450.description: Abstract The advancement of astronomical observations opens the possibility of testing our current understanding of gravitational theory in the strong-field regime and probing any deviation from general relativity. We explore to what extent compact stars predicted by non-minimal derivative coupling (NMDC) gravity theory agree with observed data.

arxiv-2405-12196.title: YASTN: Yet another symmetric tensor networks; A Python library for abelian symmetric tensor network calculations.
arxiv-2405-12196.creator: Marek M. Rams, Gabriela Wójtowicz, Aritra Sinha, Juraj Hasik
arxiv-2405-12196.description: Abstract We present an open-source tensor network Python library for quantum many-body simulations. At its core is an abelian-symmetric tensor, implemented as a sparse block structure managed by logical layer on top of dense multi-dimensional array backend. This serves as the basis for higher-level tensor networks algorithms, operating on matrix product states and projected entangled pair states, implemented here.

arxiv-2409-02166.title: Boundary SymTFT
arxiv-2409-02166.creator: Lakshya Bhardwaj, Christian Copetti, Daniel Pajer, Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
arxiv-2409-02166.description: Abstract We study properties of boundary conditions (BCs) in theories with categorical (or non-invertible) symmetries. We describe how the transformation properties, or (generalized) charges, of BCs are captured by topological BCs of Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), which is a topological field theory in one higher spacetime dimension.

arxiv-2410-06331.title: Locate-then-edit for Multi-hop Factual Recall under Knowledge Editing
arxiv-2410-06331.creator: Zhuoran Zhang, Yongxiang Li, Zijian Kan, Keyuan Cheng, Lijie Hu, Di Wang
arxiv-2410-06331.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhuoran Zhang, Yongxiang Li, Zijian Kan, Keyuan Cheng, Lijie Hu, Di Wang. The locate-then-edit paradigm has shown significant promise for knowledge editing (KE) in Large Language Models (LLMs). While previous methods perform well on single-hop fact recall tasks, they consistently struggle with multi-hop factual recall tasks involving newly edited knowledge.

arxiv-2502-10606.title: HIPPo: H arnessing I mage-to-3D P riors for Model-free Zero-shot 6D Po se Estimation Thanks: {binbin.xu,rui.heng.yang2}@h-partners.com

arxiv-2502-10606.description: Abstract This work focuses on model-free zero-shot 6D object pose estimation for robotics applications. While existing methods can estimate the precise 6D pose of objects, they heavily rely on curated CAD models or reference images, the preparation of which is a time-consuming and labor-intensive process.

arxiv-2601-05473.title: Towards Valid Student Simulation with Large Language Models
arxiv-2601-05473.creator: Zhihao Yuan, Yunze Xiao, Ming Li, Weihao Xuan, Richard Tong, Mona Diab, Tom Mitchell
arxiv-2601-05473.description: Abstract Educational innovation is often constrained by the cost, time, and ethical complexity of human-subject studies. Simulated students offer a complementary methodology: learner models that support instructional testing, data generation, teacher training, and social learning ( VanLehn et al. 1998 ; Koedinger et al. 2015 ) .

pmc-11494190.description: This study aimed to identify diagnostic gene biomarkers for colorectal cancer (CRC) by analyzing differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in tumor and adjacent normal samples across five colon cancer gene-expression profiles (GSE10950, GSE25070, GSE41328, GSE74602, GSE142279) from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database.

pmc-11506213.creator: Oana Maria Burciu, Ioan Sas, Adrian-Grigore Merce, Simona Cerbu, Aurica Elisabeta Moatar, Anca-Elena Eftenoiu, Ionut Marcel Cobec, Hans-Christian Kolberg
pmc-11506213.description: Simple SummaryThe aim of this study was to assess the impact of various factors—such as age, age at menarche, age at first childbirth, number of births, body mass index (BMI), living environment (rural vs. urban), and other factors later discussed—on the likelihood of developing breast cancer.

pmc-12674849.title: Endoscopic Retrieval of Multiple Elongated Swallowed Foreign Bodies in a Patient With Psychiatric Illness
pmc-12674849.creator: Jahnavi Pasila, Charlotte Sumner, Kehkashan Anwar, Mamoon Solkar, Nafees Qureshi
pmc-12674849.description: Foreign body ingestion is common, with most passing uneventfully through the gastrointestinal tract. However, ingested long and rigid foreign bodies pose a significant challenge for endoscopic removal from the oesophagus and stomach. This case report describes a 19-year-old woman with a history of psychiatric illness who swallowed 12 elongated foreign objects, which were successfully retrieved via esophago-gastro-duodenoscopy (EGD).

pmc-12714062.title: 512 Gbps/λ dual-polarization thin-film lithium niobate modulators based on an electro-optic equalizer
pmc-12714062.creator: Jianmin Zhang, Jian Shen, Shuxiao Wang, Zhuoyun Li, Wencheng Yue, Xin Ou, Yan Cai
pmc-12714062.description: Driven by the development of AI applications, optical communication systems experience an exponential surge in the demand for high data rates. Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) electro-optic (EO) modulators have been extensively studied and show potential for application in next-generation optical communication systems.

pmc-12737678.title: Targeting SARS-CoV-2 Mpro and PLpro by Repurposing Clinically Approved Drugs
pmc-12737678.creator: Qiaoyu Fang, Meng Lu, Derong Chen, Liangxu Xie, Wenxu Hong, Zhang Zhang, Xuqiao Hu, Daniele Focosi
pmc-12737678.description: SARS-CoV-2 virus contains two highly conserved domains, the papain-like protease (PLpro) and main protease (Mpro), which play important roles in virus replication, immune suppression, and the induction of inflammation in host tissue. In this study, we applied small-molecule chip screening, enzymatic assays, SARS-CoV-2 spike pseudotyped virus detection and molecular docking to find potential Mpro or PLpro inhibitors.

pmc-13257689.title: Mobile Health Interventions Across the Stroke Care Continuum: A Scoping Review
pmc-13257689.creator: Dahyeon Koo, Seunggyun Jeong, Kyumin Jang, Younghwan Jang, Seo Yeong Bae, Soonmi Kwon, Dougho Park
pmc-13257689.description: Stroke causes approximately 12.2 million new cases and 6.5 million deaths annually, with survivors requiring coordinated care across pre-hospital, acute, rehabilitative, and preventive phases. Mobile health (mHealth) technologies, including smartphone applications, wearable sensors, and tablet-based platforms, have shown clinical potential across these contexts, yet a structured mapping of their distribution across the full stroke care continuum is lacking.

pmc-13512917.title: Risk Stratification of Patients Being Considered for Open Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair
pmc-13512917.creator: Mitri K. Khoury, R. Trey Rogers, Hasan Aldailami, Tiziano Tallarita, Shiv Patel
pmc-13512917.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Endovascular repair (EVAR) is the default for most abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs), yet open repair (OR) remains necessary, and the decision hinges on fitness for open surgery. No standardized preoperative tool defines who is “unfit” for OR. We derived and validated a preoperative risk score for severe major adverse events (MAE) after elective OR and examined whether high-risk patients had fewer perioperative events with EVAR.
